title: Decellularization of Whole Human Heart Inside a Pressurized Pouch in an Inverted Orientation
protocol: Intravenously infuse 30,000 U heparin into the heart.
Suture cardioplegia cannula securely in the aorta and attach a clamped perfusion line.
Perforate the inferior vena cava (IVC) to vent the right heart.
Cut either the left superior pulmonary vein or the left atrial appendage to vent the left chambers of the heart.
Infuse 1 L of cardioplegia or heparinized saline into the heart.
Dissect aortic arch branches, superior vena cava (SVC), and other pulmonary veins to release the heart from any vascular or surrounding tissue attachment.
Submerge the well-heparinized heart in iced saline solution.
Inspect the donated human heart for structural damage or anatomical malformations both anteriorly and posteriorly.
Place the heart on a dissecting tray and perform an internal inspection for possible defects such as atrial septal defect (ASD), ventricular septal defect (VSD), or valve malformation.
Correct a septal defect with appropriate sutures.
Ligate the superior vena cava with 2-0 silk suture.
Ligate the inferior vena cava with 2-0 silk suture.
Dissect the aorta away from the main pulmonary artery.
Insert connectors into the aorta based on vessel diameter.
Secure the connector in the aorta with 2-0 silk sutures.
Insert connectors into the pulmonary artery based on vessel diameter.
Secure the connector in the pulmonary artery with 2-0 silk sutures.
Insert a tubing line through the left atrium toward the left ventricle using one of the pulmonary vein orifices.
Connect an infusion line to the connector placed in the aorta.
Connect an outflow line to the connector placed in the pulmonary artery.
Place the heart into a polyester pouch in inverted orientation.
Place the pouch with heart into a perfusion container and close the lid.
Connect each line to the respective ports in the rubber stopper.
Insert the rubber stopper into the lid of the perfusion container to seal the polyester pouch.
Perfuse 1x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) via the infusion port to verify outflow from the pulmonary artery and left ventricle line.
Tighten connection lines if flow is not observed.
Assemble the bioreactor and place it in an upright orientation.
Connect the infusion line, pressure-head line, pulmonary artery-outflow line, and bioreactor draining line to the rubber cap surface ports on top of the perfusion bioreactor.
Decellularize hearts under constant aortic root pressure of 120 mmHg.
Maintain left ventricle mean pressure within 14-18 mmHg throughout decellularization.
Decellularize hearts using a hypertonic solution for 4 hours (500 mM NaCl).
Proceed with hypotonic solution treatment for 2 hours (20 mM NaCl).
Continue decellularization process with sodium dodecyl sulfate (1% SDS) for 120 hours.
Wash the heart with 120 L of 1X PBS at the end.
Maintain constant pressure control during decellularization at 120 mmHg.
Infuse hypertonic solution into Ao with an average flow rate of 98.06±16.22 mL/min.
Infuse hypotonic solution into Ao with an average flow rate of 76.14±7.90 mL/min.
Infuse SDS solution into Ao with an average flow rate of 151.50±5.76 mL/min.
Wash the heart with PBS at an average flow rate of 185.24±7.10 mL/min.
Recirculate the final 60 L of 1% SDS (1 L per gram of heart weight) until end of perfusion.
Perform comparative analysis of the perfusate obtained from the PA and the LV and the infused solutions in duplicate by loading 200 μL per well in a clear bottom 96-well plate.
Read absorbance at 280 nm for each sample.
Use turbidity of clean infused reagent as control.
Add 500 mL of sterile neutralized 2.1% peracetic acid solution to 10 L of 1X PBS, leading to a 0.1% peracetic acid solution (v/v) in PBS.
Use the solution to sterilize the scaffold.
Perform coronary angiography of representative decellularized human heart after injection of contrast agent through coronary ostial cannula in main right and left coronary arteries.
Dissect the decellularized heart to obtain samples from 19 areas.
Remove the base of the heart from ventricles and dissect the ventricles into 4 equal sections.
Divide each section into anterior and posterior right ventricle (RV), anterior and posterior left ventricle (LV), and interventricular septum (IVS).
Dissect the tissue containing the apex into LV and RV for sampling.
Cut tissue samples (~15 mg of wet weight) for DNA, GAG, and SDS assays.
Digest dsDNA samples in 1 M NaOH at 65 °C for 3 hours.
Adjust pH to 7 using 10x Tris-EDTA (TE) buffer and 1 M HCl.
Quantify dsDNA using a dsDNA Assay kit with a calf thymus standard.
Read samples in duplicate using a fluorescence microplate reader at excitation 480 nm and emission 520 nm.

Obtain sulfated GAGs into solution by digesting tissue samples in papain extraction solution (0.2 M sodium phosphate buffer, EDTA disodium salt, cysteine HCl, sodium acetate, and papain) at 65 °C for 3 hours.
Measure GAG content in duplicate using a Glycosaminoglycan Assay Kit.
Lyophilize samples for SDS assay in a heated vacuum and measure dry weight.
Add 200 µL of ultrapure water to each dried sample and homogenize to extract the residual SDS into solution.
Mix this SDS solution with chloroform and a methylene blue solution (12 mg of methylene blue in 1 L of 0.01 M HCl).
Read the absorbance (655 nm) of the standards and samples in duplicate using a fluorescence microplate reader to calculate the residual SDS.
Normalize this SDS value to tissue dry weight.
Image samples from thick regions (i.e., LV, RV and septum) of human heart with nonlinear optical microscopy (NLOM).
Confirm cellular removal after decellularization through imaging.
